title: will: Decisions, Predictions and Offers
grammarTitle: will — Spontaneous Decisions, Predictions and Offers
grammarNote: "Will" используется для СПОНТАННЫХ решений (принятых прямо сейчас), ОБЩИХ ПРЕДСКАЗАНИЙ о будущем (без очевидных признаков), а также ПРЕДЛОЖЕНИЙ, ОБЕЩАНИЙ и УГРОЗ. Это главное отличие от "going to": "going to" = решение принято РАНЬШЕ; "will" = решение принимается СЕЙЧАС.

grammarTable.subject: I / He / She / We / They
grammarTable.example: I'll help you with that. (spontaneous offer)

grammarTable.subject: Will + subject?
grammarTable.example: Will you help me move? — Yes, I will.

grammarTable.subject: Positive short form
grammarTable.example: She'll call you back. / They'll be here soon.

grammarTable.subject: Negative short form
grammarTable.example: He won't arrive before 7 — he missed the bus.

rows.form: Decided at the moment of speaking
rows.example: "I'll get the door!" (just decided, not planned before)

rows.form: Often a response to what you just heard

rows.example: "I'm going to make coffee." (I already planned this before)
"I'll help you." / "I'll be there." / "I won't forget."
"I think English will be essential in her career."
"It will probably rain tomorrow." (general forecast, no clouds)

rows.form: Often with: I think / I believe / probably
rows.example: "I think she'll do well at the interview."
"Look! It's going to rain!" (I can SEE the clouds).
"I'll carry that for you." / "I'll drive you to the station."
"I'll call you as soon as I arrive." / "I won't be late."
"If you do that again, I'll report it." (conditional warning)
"She won't listen — she never does." (stubborn refusal)

grammarExtra.title: will vs going to — Quick Comparison

rows.example: "I'm going to help." (I already decided this before)
"I think life in Almaty will be exciting." (no evidence)
"Look at his CV — he's going to get the job!" (we can see the evidence)

grammarTip:
"Will" — четыре ключевых использования:
① СПОНТАННОЕ РЕШЕНИЕ: "I'll get it!" — решил ПРЯМО СЕЙЧАС.
② ПРЕДСКАЗАНИЕ без очевидных признаков: "I think it will rain." — общее мнение о будущем.
③ ОБЕЩАНИЕ: "I'll call you tomorrow." — обязательство.
④ ПРЕДЛОЖЕНИЕ ПОМОЧЬ: "I'll carry that for you." — ненавязчивое предложение.

💡 Ключ: если решение принято ДО разговора → going to. Если принято ПРЯМО СЕЙЧАС → will.

⚠️ "won't" = will not. Всегда одна форма: I/you/he/she/we/they + will (НЕ меняется по лицам!).

exercises.text: "Amir, can you help me?" — "___ I help you right now!"
exercises.hint: Spontaneous offer made right now → "will". "I'll help you!" ✅ (not planned before)
Promise using "will" negative: won't + base verb. "I won't be late." ✅

exercises.text: "I think English ___ be even more important in 2030."
exercises.hint: "I think" + general prediction about the future → "will". No specific evidence — just a belief.

exercises.text: "She will not" and "she won't" have the same meaning.
exercises.hint: "will not" = "won't" — exactly the same meaning. "won't" is just the contracted spoken form.

exercises.text: There's no milk. "Don't worry — I ___ go and get some."
exercises.hint: Spontaneous decision made right now in response to the situation → "will". "I'll go and get some." ✅

exercises.instruction: Which use of "will" is in this sentence: "I'll be there by 7, I promise."
exercises.hint: "I promise" confirms this is a promise. "I'll be there" = a commitment about the future.

exercises.text: "She ___ probably be an excellent researcher. She's incredibly dedicated."
exercises.hint: Prediction based on a personal belief about her character → "will/'ll". "She'll probably be excellent."

exercises.instruction: Which sentence is a SPONTANEOUS OFFER?
exercises.hint: "I'll make you tea!" = spontaneous offer decided right now as a response to the situation.

exercises.text: Kamila has already registered and paid. "___ attend the conference in June."
exercises.hint: Already registered and paid = decision made before → "going to". "She's going to attend." ✅

exercises.text: "Will" changes form for different subjects: I will / she wills / they willes.
exercises.hint: "will" NEVER changes! I will / she will / they will — always the same form for all subjects.

exercises.text: "___ you help me with my essay?" — "Of course I ___!"
exercises.hint: Question: "Will you...?" → Short positive answer: "Of course I will!" (not "going to")

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct sentence for a PROMISE.
opts: "I was going to be on time."
exercises.hint: "I'll... I promise!" = classic promise structure. "will" for promises and commitments.

questions.text: "I'll get the door!" — What use of "will" is this?
questions.hint: "I'll get the door" = decided right now, spontaneously, in response to someone knocking.
"won't" can express refusal or stubborn unwillingness: "She won't listen — she never does."

questions.text: "There's no one to give her a lift. — I ___ (take) her!"
questions.hint: Spontaneous offer: deciding right now to help → "will". "I'll take her!" ✅
Short negative answer: "No, I won't." (will not → contracted).

questions.text: "I think technology ___ change education completely in 20 years."
"I wills help" is correct because "will" is a verb.
questions.hint: "will" NEVER adds -s. All subjects: I will / she will / they will. "wills" does not exist!

questions.text: Choose the sentence that is an OFFER:
questions.hint: "I'll cook dinner for you!" = spontaneous offer made right now to help someone.

questions.text: Contrast: "I'll go to the shop" vs "I'm going to go to the shop."
questions.hint: "I'll go" = just decided now. "I'm going to go" = already had this plan before this conversation.

questions.text: "She ___ (call) you as soon as she arrives. I promise."
questions.hint: Promise about the future → "will". "She'll call you as soon as she arrives." ✅

questions.text: "They ___ probably ___ us later." Choose the correct form.
questions.hint: "probably" + general prediction → "will". "They will probably join us." ✅ "will + base verb".

questions.text: "Look — he's going to ___ vs "I think he'll ___." Difference?
questions.hint: "going to" = we can SEE/KNOW the outcome (evidence). "will" = a belief or prediction without visible proof.

questions.text: Rustam: "There's no coffee." Kamila: "Don't worry — I ___ (make) some!"
questions.hint: Spontaneous response to a situation → "will". "I'll make some!" — decided right now.

questions.text: "I won't tell anyone about this." What use is "won't" here?
questions.hint: "I won't tell" = a promise not to do something. Negative promise using "won't".
✅ "She will study harder." — "will" + BASE VERB. Never "will + past form"!

questions.text: "___ she come to the party?" — "I'm not sure — she ___ maybe."
questions.hint: "Will she come?" = prediction/question about future. "She will maybe." = uncertain prediction.

questions.text: Choose the correct use: "I think life in Almaty ___ exciting."
questions.hint: "I think..." + future opinion/belief without evidence → "will be". "I think life will be exciting."
